name: Narim
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Moges Yigezu 2001-2002, A comparative study of the phonetics and phonology of Surmic languages (PhD thesis, ULB; covers Narim/Larim; cited on Glottolog); not fetchable.

sources.citation: Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 10 (2012) and 11 (SIL South Sudan).
sources.note: No Laarim article in either volume (only the back-list citing Lokonobei & de Jong 1989).

sources.citation: SIL International publication record for SILEWP 2011-012 (www.sil.org/resources/publications/entry/42939), abstract.
sources.note: Abstract: 'Laarim... has High and Low level tone and the tone-bearing unit is the syllable'; no stress.

sources.citation: Stirtz, Timothy M. 2011. Laarim (loh) Tone. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2011-012. Dallas: SIL International. 91 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 0 (p.4): 'Laarim has High and Low level tone and the tone-bearing unit is the syllable'; five tone melodies on noun roots, three on verb roots, automatic downstep; whole paper is tone + segmental morphophonology. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur (only 'acute or grave accent' as an orthographic diacritic, p.~25).

sources.citation: Joseph, Clement Lopeyok; Lochule, Michael Vorgol; Lolar, Joseph Celestine; et al. 2013. Laarim Grammar Book. 4th edition. Juba: SIL-Sudan. 142 pp. (also SIL archive copy, archives/58705)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Spelling rules (heavy/light = ATR vowels) and tone explained for nominative marking ('Tone is the difference in pitch...', p.~29); no mention of stress or accent anywhere (grep + reading).

sources.citation: Laarim Translation and Literacy Project [T. Stirtz]. 2014. Laarim Consonant and Vowel Book (LaarimVowelBookMar14). Juba: SIL South Sudan. 33 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; 'Syllables' section (p.5) only divides words into 'beats'; consonant/vowel inventories, heavy/light vowels, doubled consonants.

sources.citation: Joseph, Clement Lopeyok et al. 2013. Laarim Discourse Grammar Book. Juba: SIL-Sudan. 201 pp.
sources.note: Nothing (discourse grammar; glossary repeats syllable/consonant/vowel definitions only).

sources.citation: Stirtz, Timothy M. 2012. Polar Tone of Laarim, a Surmic Language of Sudan. In M. Marlo et al. (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 42nd Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 79-89. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; phoneme charts and tone only ('The syllable is the tone bearing unit and usually only one tone is assigned per syllable', sec. 2.2).

sources.citation: Joseph, Clement Lopeyok & Timothy M. Stirtz. 2010/2011. Laarim-English Dictionary (Introduction, 6 pp. + entries, 22 pp.). Juba: SIL-Sudan.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; entries carry isolation tone patterns e.g. [LH]; intro explains tone marking only.

sources.citation: Lokonobei, Lino Locek & Nicky de Jong. 1989. On the position of Boya in relation to Murle and Didinga. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 6: 77-94. (SIL-Sudan facsimile 2005; scanned pp. 77-94)
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistic comparison plus a ~280-item Boya/Murle/Didinga wordlist without tone or stress marking.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Laarim language' (checked for phonology section / references).
sources.note: No phonology section; cites only Ethnologue and Stirtz 2011.

sources.citation: Stirtz, Timothy & Clement Lopeyok Joseph. 2009. Phonology Write-up of Laarim. Unpublished manuscript, SIL, Nairobi.

sources.note: The segmental + suprasegmental phonology statement underlying Stirtz 2011 and the literacy books; an SIL phonology write-up normally has a section on stress/tone and syllable structure.

sources.citation: Yigezu, Moges. 2005. Aspects of Murle phonology. Journal of Ethiopian Studies 38: 115-129.

sources.note: Closest sister language (Didinga-Murle group) by the same phonetician; may contain a general Southwest-Surmic statement on stress vs tone that he applies to Narim in the thesis.

sources.citation: de Jong, Nicky. 2004. Didinga orthography. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 145-164; and Odden, David 1983. Aspects of Didinga phonology and morphology. In Bender (ed.) Nilo-Saharan Language Studies, 148-176.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not fetched sources
sources.note: Didinga is Narim's closest relative (83% lexical similarity, Lokonobei & de Jong 1989); these give explicit prosody statements for the Didinga-Longarim node, useful as identity-adjacent evidence only (different glottocode didi1258).

sources.citation: Yigezu, Moges. 2001[-2002]. A comparative study of the phonetics and phonology of Surmic languages. PhD dissertation, Universite Libre de Bruxelles. vi+420 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only full phonetic/phonological treatment covering Narim alongside the other Surmic languages; the earlier scan named it as the likely stress source; a comparative phonology is the most likely place for an explicit statement on stress vs. tone in Narim.
